steps.content: Then, cheers and footsteps begin to echo, getting ever closer.

Children laugh and jostle one another as they race through the orphanage corridor. An elderly woman wearing reading glasses passes by with a large tray of freshly risen dough, nearly knocked off balance by the little rascals under her.
Fortunately, someone quickly steps up from behind and steadies her.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Look out! Annie, stop leading everyone on a rampage. Have you finished your arithmetic homework?

steps.speaker: Little Boy A
steps.content: We finished ages ago, Clementine! Annie came in last, and Searle got first place again.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: I thought so. Annie, go get your teddy bear back. Searle's not going to do your homework just because you let him play with it for a bit.

steps.speaker: Little Girl A
steps.content: Then come give it back to me yourself!

steps.speaker: Little Boy B
steps.content: Hey, get back here!
The children's voices grow louder, each trying to outdo the last. Clementine crosses her arms and shrugs in resignation.
Suddenly, a large, rough hand swoops down, snatches up the teddy bear, and hoists it high into the air.

steps.speaker: Little Girl A
steps.content: Give it back... William?!

steps.speaker: William
steps.content: That's enough. No running indoors. If you keep this up, I'm giving this bear to someone who knows how to behave.

steps.speaker: Children
steps.content: We won't do it again!

steps.speaker: Little Girl A
steps.content: I... I won't do it again either!
William's stern warning sends the children into a panic, tears welling up in their eyes. Just then, a teasing voice cuts through the tension.

steps.speaker: Allison
steps.content: Oh! Everyone's here. William, weren't you planning to confess to my sister today? Why are you still here, lecturing the kids? Don't tell me... are you chickening out again?

steps.speaker: William
steps.content: Huh? How do you all know—

Allison works as a sand ship crew member to make a living and is rarely home. She takes the tray from the old woman's hands, grinning. She's visiting for once, and the first thing she does is send William flushed with just one sentence.
What mortifies him even more is that Mrs. Jones, who's standing nearby, is also wearing a knowing smile.

steps.speaker: Mrs. Jones
steps.content: I've lost count of how many times you've rehearsed for it, dear. Just look at you, walking around with such a long face every day because Elizabeth is away.

steps.speaker: Allison
steps.content: Oh my! I see... looks like you'll need a little <color=#fb9259>push</color>, huh? What should we do at times like this?

steps.speaker: Little Girl A
steps.content: Oh! I know! We should say—

steps.speaker: Children
steps.content: You can do it, William!
Amid the burst of laughter, William tugs his hat down to hide his reddened face.

steps.speaker: William
steps.content: Come on, Allison! This was supposed to be a surprise! As for you rascals...

He puts on a stern face, points two fingers at his eyes, then at the children—the classic "I'm watching you" gesture. The kids instantly cover their mouths before walking obediently toward the reading room in a line, hand in hand.

steps.speaker: Allison
steps.content: Need my help? The full package costs just three hundred DisCoins! Romantic coaching and atmosphere management included!

steps.speaker: William
steps.content: Please don't. I'll only be more nervous if there are people watching...
William's gaze sweeps around the room before finally settling on Clementine. She spreads her hands, as if to say she has nothing to do with this.

steps.speaker: William
steps.content: Clementine! You're the most reliable one here. Help me out and go tell the kids a story or something to keep them distracted. Elizabeth's in town for once, so I can't let this opportunity go. I'm going to practice a few more times. Just don't let them spill the beans!

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Of course. I won't disturb you. Take your time.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Though... I did take that bouquet out from under the stove for you. It was starting to smell more like roasted chicken than flowers.

steps.speaker: William
steps.content: When did you find it?!
Sensing William's growing frustration, the children scatter in an instant.

Warm sunlight fills the hallway, and dust drifts through the air. The children race down the corridor, laughing, then pause at a doorframe to measure their heights. However, none of them can reach the mark at the very top—the one labeled Clementine.
It's not a large place, nor a wealthy one, but it's clean and warm. This is home to everyone here.
[Scene Change]
The air carries the faint sweetness of buckwheat flowers. The children gather quietly around Clementine, who sits on the sofa.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Now then... who remembers where we left off last time?

steps.speaker: Little Girl A
steps.content: We were on an adventure in the Redwood Kingdom, but the demon bear in the forest tricked us and trapped us in a spider's lair!

steps.speaker: Little Boy B
steps.content: We were all strung up in spider silk, but Allison the mage is still waiting for news from the expedition team!

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Very good. It seems you were all paying close attention, my brave adventurers.
The young woman holds a handwritten notebook, weaving a fantastical world of wonder and mystery for the children.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: After that day...

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: As the morning sun broke through the mist and illuminated the cave, you were finally able to cut through the thick spider cocoons using the enchanted blade Allison tossed in. Daylight painted the forest in an emerald green, the trees no longer sinister and foreboding. The spiders grew drowsy and retreated into their nests.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Annie, clutching the fluffy bear paw, blew the spiders a kiss. The adventurers set off once more into the dawn.

Mrs. Jones is the queen of the Redwood Kingdom, the grumpy William is a kindhearted police officer who struggles with words, the mischievous Alison is an enigmatic mage, and the young adventurers each possess their own special talents.
The children are completely absorbed, gasping and exclaiming every now and then. When the adventurers face danger, they even debate among themselves as to what will happen next.
In Clementine's stories, the heroes always defeat the villains, and justice always prevails. It's a theme that carries through to her later works.
If only... she could keep telling stories like this forever...
[Scene Change]
The fire doesn't take long to consume everything.
No one knows where the fire started. The only thing that's known is that the old furniture, too worn for use, and donations that the orphanage just received caught on fire.

The flames then slowly devoured everything combustible until they reached the kitchen. The gas exploded with a deafening roar. The massive old tree became engulfed in a sea of fire, its light painting the moon crimson.
Clementine charges into the inferno in desperation, only to be driven back again and again by the bursting flames and explosions.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Annie, Searle? Nana, Viola... cough, cough... where are you?

The children cry out from within the rooms, now choked with smoke. Clementine, wrapped in a blanket soaked in ice water, searches frantically for a way in. The wail of police and fire engine sirens feels unbearably distant and slow.
Through the haze, a strange figure lingers by the outer wall. The moment they see Clementine, they immediately turn around, vault over a fallen beam, and bolt into the forest.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Hey, it's dangerous over there—
But then, a terrible thought strikes her, hitting like a sledgehammer against nerves already pushed to the breaking point.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Wait... Stop right there! Who are you? Why were you there?!
Rage nearly blinds her. She pursues the figure without hesitation. That is, until a faint cry reaches her ears from behind the fallen beam.
Clementine... it hurts... it hurts so... bad...
Clementine freezes. Torn between two impossible choices, she ultimately turns back in a panic. By the time she looks again, the figure has vanished.
[Still the scene of the fire]

The wall is charred. The flames grow fiercer by the second. She's finally pinpointed the source of the crying—it's coming from a tiny window. A child that young could never reach it alone, which means someone must have lifted her up.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Don't be scared! I'm here! Grab my hand!!!
Clementine musters every ounce of strength to move the burning beam, stepping on the sections not yet consumed by flames. Finally, she grasps the small hand.

The roar of the flames becomes mingled with shrieks and anguished cries. Another explosion rocks the building. She crashes to the ground with the child in her arms, rolling until the flames on her body go out.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Ngh... Cough, cough cough...
The small orphanage, a home filled with laughter and dreams, becomes a towering pillar of flame under the curtain of the night... A "Burning Redwood."
[Scene Change]

steps.speaker: TV Host
steps.content: Following the Redwood incident that shocked Eastside, the Eastside Public Security Bureau immediately launched an investigation and arrested a suspect on the 23rd of this month.

steps.speaker: TV Host
steps.content: The suspect claims to have been intoxicated and has no recollection of committing the crime. A public trial will be held on the 30th of this month at the Eastside People's Court.

steps.speaker: Concerned Citizen
steps.content: It's truly terrible... The orphanage walls were burnt clean through. They'd collapse at the slightest touch. What a tragedy... No one even knows how many children perished in that fire...

steps.speaker: Concerned Citizen
steps.content: I heard the youngest were only five or six years old... One child was rescued, but there were several others in the same room who didn't make it...

steps.speaker: Tabloid Reporter
steps.content: The culprit? Yeah, he's already convicted. Guy was confused the whole time. If you ask me, he had nothing to do with it. Probably just a guy they pushed out to take the fall.

steps.speaker: Tabloid Reporter
steps.content: What else is new? End of the year's coming up, everyone's looking to sweep the big problems under the rug and make the small ones disappear. The Public Security Bureau's in a rush to close cases. Tsk, tsk, tsk... This one goes deep, I tell you...
[Montage sequence: Cycle through several different background images showing the various places Clementine has been]

<i>The days that followed felt surreal. Almost like someone had pressed a fast-forward button.

The orphanage was gone, naturally. The case was stated to be an accident, but that figure from that day haunted Clementine's thoughts, robbing her of sleep night after night.

People came in droves—angry, pitying, morbidly curious... Their gazes would inevitably drift toward her, meeting her eyes before awkwardly looking away.

<i>She seemed to have matured overnight, yet she was still so young. So powerless.

The adults sought the truth behind the fire, boarding a sand ship called the Praeva, and then... they never came back.

Clementine was an orphan once more.

<i>Justice and law could no longer be trusted. If she wanted to find the truth, she would have to seek a different way.

And so, she began weaving stories once more.

She created countless false names and identities for herself—a fallen Eastside noble, a private detective who specialized in dirty work, a smuggler with ties to the black market.

Through these disguises, she slipped into the underworld and slowly began to uncover leads.

<i>A name from the list of the orphanage's former sponsors.

An organization concealing the darkest secrets buried in the depths of Eastside.

They profited off of and covered for each other. To them, both human lives and money are but numbers. There were countless more tragedies like Redwood, all swept under the rug.

<i>But those forces were too deeply entrenched. Someone as insignificant as her could never hope to touch the true culprit. She nearly lost her life just trying.

Then, in her darkest hour, someone extended a hand.

She had already lost everything. So even if the price was her life... it would still be worth it, wouldn't it?
[Try using that blue dream dynamic background, or find something more suitable]
She picks up her pen once more—not to weave fairy tales for children, but to pursue vengeance. She becomes the characters in her own stories, spinning webs with her words to ensnare her prey.
But sometimes, in her dreams, an endless road would appear.

At first, the surroundings are familiar. There are the friends and mentors she sees regularly, her editors at the publishing house, the streets she knows, her home, the shops and restaurants she frequents.
She walks faster and faster, almost breaking into a sprint, while a distant voice echoes endlessly in the back of her mind.
Run faster. Faster!
Until everything falls into silence and darkness spreads without end. The voice grows louder, clearer. It's Clementine's own voice.
Run faster—save the children trapped in those rooms before the flames swallow the hallway.
Faster—chase them down, they're just by the wall near the flames. You could have caught the culprit right then and there.
Run faster. Faster. Grab the Director's sleeve at the dock, muster the courage to ask just one more question. "Where are you going? What are you going to do?"
It's fine even if I have to do it in secret... just let me go along with you.
She regrets it time and time again. If only she had chased after the true culprit instead of saving people, would things have turned out differently?

steps.speaker: Mrs. Jones
steps.content: Clementine, you're the one we worry about least... Even when we're not around, you must take care of yourself...
I'm the only one left... the only one... all alone...

But there are no what-ifs. The ending was already written. The story of Redwood Orphanage was destined to end there. Time drags her forward like a viscous tide, washing her ashore again and again, yet never letting her go.
Clementine stumbles forward, step by step, until her fury burns to ashes and her guilt erodes to sand. In the end, even pain itself grows numb. Nothing remains but dying embers and fading sparks.
She continues to burn in defiance, walking forward, as the world around her turns hollow and pure...
And finally, even her hatred is spent. She turns around, only to find herself surrounded by nothing but the void.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Where... was I going again?

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: ...Where... can I even go...?
From within the void, a voice calls out.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: ...Clementine, come back!
A hand reaches out to grab her, but passes straight through her fading form.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Clementine, stop! Your vengeance is complete! You don't have to go any further!

Clementine's existence grows fainter, her body becoming more transparent, as if she's disappearing alongside all those memories. Someone calls out to her desperately, but it doesn't seem to reach her. She simply continues forward, numb to it all.
A hand reaches out, gently pulling Hella's hand away from her face.
steps.female_content: Her desperation mounts. Finally, she makes up her mind. In the next instant, spikes burst forth from where their bodies connect—

steps.content: [Release the shackles effect]
[Scene Transition: Back to Reality]

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Clementine!!!
You jolt awake. The warmth and touch of human skin radiates from your right palm.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Don't worry... I'm not going anywhere now.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: You're quite strong, you know. You're gripping my arm so hard it hurts.
The battle has ended. The ground is covered in traces of combat. In the illusion, you witnessed ten years of Clementine's life in a haze. Yet, in reality, mere seconds have passed.
Clementine has no energy left to speak or smile. She stumbles forward, still acting as though nothing is wrong. She pulls you forward a few steps, just like she did in the illusion.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Shh, don't speak. Fighting while protecting someone is far more exhausting than fighting alone. Let me rest for a moment.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: ...I'll leave the cleanup in your hands.
Finally, her body gives out, and she collapses.
